newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Burma formally applies to join ASEAN - Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Burma formally applies to join ASEAN - Malaysia.

text.p: Burma has made a formal application for full membership of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi said on Tuesday.

Burmese Foreign Minister Ohn Gyaw handed over the application last month during a visit by Burmese junta leader General Than Shwe and top members of his ruling council, the national news agency Bernama quoted Abdullah as saying.
Malaysia is the current chairman of ASEAN, which also groups Indonesia, the Philippines, Brunei, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Abdullah said he was optimistic Burma would be accepted, judging from statements by the other members and also because ASEAN aims eventually to have all 10 Southeast Asia countries in the group.
Laos and Cambodia are set to join ASEAN next year.

Burma was admitted as an official observer of ASEAN in July. Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad suggested during Than Shwe's visit in August that Rangoon could be made a full member as early as next year.

ASEAN follows a policy of "constructive engagement" with Burma, which says that reforming Rangoon stands a better chance if the ruling generals are engaged in constant dialogue within the group than if they are left in isolation.
Burma has been treated as a virtual pariah by ASEAN's Western trading partners for its suppression of a pro-democracy movement led by Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.
